note: Every layer and reading in CAIRN, with the mission, instrument, product and provider it came from.

entries.layer: Terrain elevation (3D surface, slope, routing grid)
entries.product: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation HiRISE DTM mosaic, 1 m/post (JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_1m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_blend40)
entries.usedFor: 3D terrain mesh (2 m), per-pixel relief lighting (full 1 m), slope map, metabolic cost of every step, impassable-ground mask

entries.product: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation HiRISE orthorectified image mosaic, 25 cm/px (JEZ_hirise_soc_006_orthoMosaic_25cm_Eqc_latTs0_lon0_first)
entries.usedFor: Ground texture at the full 25 cm resolution (50 cm on GPUs limited to 4096 px textures), sand-ripple detection
entries.note: HiRISE is a single-band (grey) image here; the Mars colour in the 3D view is a display tint, not measured colour.

entries.product: THEMIS Night IR controlled mosaic of the Nili Planum / Jezero region, ~100 m/px (distributed with USGS SIM 3464)
entries.provider: USGS Astrogeology Science Center / Arizona State University
entries.usedFor: Thermal layer; fused with HiRISE to flag loose sand (sand is cold at night, bedrock stays warm)
entries.note: Native resolution is ~100 m, so this layer is smooth at walking scale.

entries.instrument: Map compiled from CTX, HiRISE, THEMIS and HRSC data
entries.product: USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3464 — Geologic map of Jezero crater and the Nili Planum region, Mars (Sun & Stack, 2020), 1:75,000
entries.credit: Sun, V.Z., and Stack, K.M., 2020, USGS SIM 3464
entries.usedFor: Geology layer and the rock unit shown under the cursor and at each stop
entries.note: Mapped at 1:75,000, so unit boundaries are approximate at walking scale.

entries.product: MTRDR summary parameters FRT00005C5E_07_SU166J_MTR3 (18 m/px) + HRL000040FF_07_SU183J_MTR3 (36 m/px): OLINDEX3, D2300, MIN2295_2480
entries.provider: NASA Planetary Data System, Geosciences Node
entries.usedFor: Mineral layer and the CRISM line in the map probe
entries.note: CRISM imaged the north-east quarter of the walk area. Strength is scaled to these observations (Viviano-Beck et al. 2014 parameters).

entries.instrument: HiRISE image, HiRISE DTM, THEMIS night IR
entries.product: Computed by CAIRN (data-pipeline/build_site.py): ripple texture in the HiRISE image and DTM, weighted by THEMIS night-time temperature
entries.credit: Derived from NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/ASU/USGS data
entries.usedFor: Extra walking energy on sand (×2.1 at full strength) and slower walking speed
entries.note: This is our own analysis, not an official NASA product.

entries.product: Computed by CAIRN: share of the sky blocked by terrain within 260 m of each point (HiRISE DTM), weighted by a cos² zenith dependence of the surface dose
entries.credit: Derived from NASA/JPL-Caltech/University of Arizona/USGS data
entries.usedFor: Sky shielding layer, dose along the route, nearest natural cover during the storm
entries.note: Model, not a measurement: the zenith exponent is an assumption.

entries.product: Mars 2020 Terrain Relative Navigation CTX DTM mosaic, 20 m/post (JEZ_ctx_B_soc_008_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_20m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0) and orthorectified image mosaic, 6 m/px (JEZ_ctx_B_soc_008_orthoMosaic_6m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0)
entries.usedFor: The 16 km of terrain around the walk area in the 3D view (tone-matched and height-blended to the HiRISE data at the seam), and the regional map in the mission briefing
Global locator in the mission briefing
Position of every EVA stop, the rover track on the map, and the regional traverse

entries.product: Mars 2020 raw images feed — images taken at the same rover positions as the EVA stops
entries.usedFor: "What you will see" photos when planning and on arrival

entries.product: MEDA derived pressure and calibrated TIRS air / ground temperature, sol 1215
entries.provider: NASA Planetary Data System, Atmospheres Node
entries.usedFor: Pressure, air temperature and ground temperature readouts during the EVA

entries.product: MSL-M-RAD-3-RDR-V1.0, sols 4189–4194 (18–24 May 2024), detector E dose rate
entries.provider: NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Plasma Interactions Node
entries.usedFor: Background dose rate and the measured points of the storm replay
entries.note: Curiosity is in Gale crater, about 3,700 km from Jezero. The archive holds 2–4 hours of dosimetry per sol, so the first ~13 hours of the 20 May 2024 storm are not in it. That gap is filled by a clearly labelled model scaled to NASA's reported total of 8,100 micrograys.

entries.instrument: DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information)
entries.provider: NASA CCMC / Moon to Mars Space Weather Analysis Office
entries.usedFor: The real eruption record and alert text shown in the storm replay
